question: If a substance loses hydrogen during a reaction, it is said to be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**oxidised**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• If a substance loses hydrogen during a reaction, it is said to be **oxidised**.
 
• Oxidation is a process that involves the loss of electrons or an increase in oxidation state by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• In the context of hydrogen transfer, oxidation specifically refers to the loss of hydrogen atoms.
 
• Conversely, reduction refers to the gain of hydrogen atoms or the gain of electrons.
 
• Understanding the concepts of oxidation and reduction is fundamental in the study of redox reactions in chemistry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The terms oxidation and reduction originally referred to reactions involving the addition or removal of oxygen, respectively.
 
• These definitions have since been broadened to include the transfer of electrons and hydrogen atoms.
 
• Redox reactions are essential in various chemical processes, including metabolism, combustion, and corrosion.
 
• Oxidising agents are substances that can accept electrons, while reducing agents are substances that can donate electrons.
